To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

continuous-domain multiple comparison methods are often superior to discrete-domain methods and, when there are many parameters, the discrete- and continuous-domains are not as different as one might think.

(1) continuous-domain approaches are useful in multiple comparisons problems with many parameters; (2) the continuous domain approach is a generalization of the discrete domain approach; (3) the discrete domain approach may be conservative when the number of parameters is large.

(1) the continuous-domain approach is more powerful than the discrete-domain approach; (2) the continuous-domain SCR is not conservative when the number of parameters is infinite; (3) the SCR for the discrete case is not necessarily the same as that for the continuous case; and (4) a continuous domain approach is better than a discrete approach even if the number of parameters in the discrete approach is small.

the development of multiple comparison procedures for continuous domain problems and the exploration of connections between continuous- and discrete-domain approaches.
